subject: physics
title: The Photoelectric Effect
welcome_lead: Shine light on a metal and meet Einstein's photon theory at the work function.
meta_desc: A-Level Quantum adventure on the photoelectric effect and photon energy.
final_note: No emission below the threshold frequency, no matter how bright the light.

concepts.def: Discrete quantum of EM radiation, E = h f.
Minimum energy to free an electron.
½ m v²_max = h f − φ.

walkthroughs.body_html: Each photon delivers energy hf in a single interaction with one electron. If hf > φ, the electron escapes with KE = hf − φ. Intensity controls photon count, not energy.
Below threshold frequency f₀ = φ/h, no electrons are emitted, no matter how intense the light. This killed the wave-only theory of light.
Apply reverse voltage until current stops. Then eV_s = KE_max = hf − φ. Plotting V_s vs f gives a line of gradient h/e.

mcqs.q: What is the threshold frequency in the photoelectric effect?
options: The minimum frequency of light required to eject electrons from a given metal — it equals the work function divided by Planck's constant.
The frequency at which photons travel at the speed of light.
Photon energy depends on how fast the photon is moving relative to the source.
The minimum intensity of light needed to eject electrons.

mcqs.q: Why does increasing the intensity of light below the threshold frequency not eject electrons?
options: Enough low-frequency photons should eventually eject an electron if you wait long enough.
Each photon's energy is below the work function; many low-energy photons can't combine to eject an electron.
Photon energy depends on how fast the photon is moving relative to the source.
Low-frequency light doesn't have enough mass to push electrons out of the metal.

mcqs.q: What determines the energy of a single photon?
options: Low-frequency light doesn't have enough mass to push electrons out of the metal.
Photon energy depends on how fast the photon is moving relative to the source.
A brighter light has higher-energy photons because intensity makes each photon more energetic.
Its frequency (E = hf) — only frequency, not intensity.
